summary:
MUNE (Lunar Mission Navigator) is an integrated decision-support platform designed for navigating the hazardous terrain of the Moon's South Pole. Choosing viable lunar landing sites is exceptionally challenging due to extreme crater slopes, perpetual darkness, and intermittent Earth communication windows. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by Team Astro X Bound, MUNE unifies fragmented mission data into an end-to-end interactive workflow. 

By ingesting NASA LOLA altimetry and NAIF SPICE ephemerides, the platform calculates 3D elevation profiles, real-time solar illumination, direct-to-Earth communication links, and translunar transfer trajectories. A multi-criteria decision engine evaluates candidate sites against customizable engineering constraints, generating automated safety rankings and exportable mission reports. MUNE also features real-time powered descent physics and an interactive Moon Run arcade game, bridging rigorous planetary science with intuitive visual analytics to make lunar landings safer and mission planning smarter.
details:
TEAM ASTRO X BOUND

Team Members: Seetha Lakshmi R, Mari Aishwarya M, Anto Varshilin T

Challenge: Commercial Lunar Landing Site Selection / Lunar Mission Navigation

Full Demo Video (3-Min): https://youtu.be/nCBEbWd_vRs

Open Source Code: https://github.com/AntoLin-cyber/MUNE-Lunar-Mission-Navigator

1. WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

MUNE (Lunar Mission Navigator) unifies disparate lunar datasets into a single, cohesive web platform for mission architects:

- 3D Terrain Analysis (NASA LOLA): Imports high-resolution Digital Elevation Models (DEM) to generate interactive 3D terrain meshes. It computes slope gradients, surface roughness indices, and 360-degree horizon obstruction masks across candidate sites.

- Orbital Mechanics & Launch Opportunities: Simulates translunar injection (TLI) transfer trajectories and delta-v propulsion budgets.

- Solar & Communication Ephemerides (NAIF SPICE & JPL DE421): Calculates real-time solar elevation angles, illumination duration, and direct line-of-sight communication windows to Earth Ground Stations.

- Multi-Criteria Decision Engine: Compares candidate landing sites against user-defined engineering thresholds (slope limits, continuous sunlight hours, comms blackout limits), rendering automated PASS/FAIL status and rankings.

- Powered Descent Simulation & Moon Run Game: Simulates real-time landing thrust physics to candidate landing pads and features "Moon Run"—an interactive low-gravity rover navigation mini-game.

- Mission Export: Generates comprehensive mission briefing summaries and downloadable site reports.

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Eliminates Tool Fragmentation: Replaces separate CAD, orbital mechanics, and GIS tools with a single unified dashboard.

- Minimizes Mission Risk: Identifies dangerous crater slopes and communication blackouts before final site commitment.

- Accelerates Mission Planning: Enables rapid trade-off studies across multiple Artemis-era South Pole candidate sites.

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

MUNE provides commercial lunar lander missions, space agencies, and researchers with an open-source, accessible toolkit to plan safe touchdowns at the lunar South Pole. It bridges complex orbital and topographic science with intuitive visual interaction for both aerospace professionals and educational outreach.

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (WebGL 3D graphics), Web Audio API, Canvas API.

- Backend & Data Science: Python 3.12, NumPy, Pandas, Astropy, SciPy.

- Data Ingestion & Formats: NASA LOLA Gridded Data Records (GeoTIFF/IMG), JPL DE421 binary SPK kernels, NAIF SPICE Toolkit.

- Production & Video: FFmpeg, PIL, ElevenLabs Neural Text-to-Speech.

5. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

MUNE bridges scientific accuracy with intuitive gamification. Rather than static numerical tables, users can visually explore 3D crater terrain, test real-time descent trajectories, and play the Moon Run arcade game to intuitively experience lunar gravity, crater collision physics, and rover mobility constraints.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Topography: Surface slope thresholds (<10°), boulder hazards, and crater depth.

- Power: Solar incidence angles, permanent shadow regions (PSRs), and peaks of eternal light.

- Telemetry & Comms: Direct Earth line-of-sight and relay occultation blackout intervals.

- Spacecraft Performance: Thrust-to-weight margins, delta-v fuel budgets, and landing descent velocity.
